summary: CI runners lose job-level permissions during credential rollforward causing blocked release jobs
description:
Issue summary:
During an automated credential rollforward of CI service identities, a subset of self-hosted release runners began receiving limited job-level permissions (missing repo:write / artifact:upload scopes). Affected runners accepted jobs but failed at job initialization when trying to fetch secrets or upload artifacts.

Impact:
- Multiple release pipelines for core services (release/*) are blocked across us-east-1 for ~2 hours during the window.
- Customers were not exposed, but several production deploys and hotfixes were delayed.
- Engineers observed opaque 'permission denied' failures in job setup step and 403s when contacting our artifact storage service.

Observed timeframe:
- First detection: 2024-11-15T08:12:00 UTC
- Bulk symptom window: 08:12–09:40 UTC (partial recovery after manual intervention)

What changed recently:
- Automated credential rollforward for ephemeral GCP service accounts (rollforward job executed as part of monthly key hygiene).
- Vault rewrap operation touched a subset of runner bindings two hours prior.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1
- Self-hosted runners in GKE node pool 'runners-prod-eu-1' (note: mixed kube region names present in config)

Steps to reproduce (local / reproducible path):
1) Trigger the same rollforward script in staging with an account that has the old and new key versions mounted.
2) Observe the runner registration flow updating credentials.
3) Run a sample job that requires 'artifact:write' and 'repo:read'.
4) Job fails with 403 on artifact store and exits before steps execute.

Failure logs (representative snippets):
- runner-init.log: "oauth: token exchange succeeded but scopes missing: [artifact:write]"
- artifact-uploader: "PUT /artifacts/upload 403 Forbidden (missing write scope)"
- k8s events: "Secret mount failed: forbidden - iam unable to bind serviceaccount"
steps_to_reproduce: Run cvg-rollforward script against staging vault with non-matching binding template
Register runner and attempt to run a job that uploads artifacts
Observe token scopes returned from token-introspect endpoint
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: During the rollforward process we rotated keys and briefly served tokens minted by a new token-issuer that hadn’t yet been propagated to the runner-authz-cache. Runners accepted tokens but token introspection returned a reduced scope set because the binding metadata lookup failed with a datastore timeout.

What we checked:
- Vault audit logs show rewrap completed at 2024-11-15T07:55:21 UTC for the affected path.
- Token-issuer logs show token creation with expected scopes at 07:56:02 UTC.
- Authz-cache (redis) had a spike in eviction/failed lookups between 08:08–08:15 UTC coinciding with high write ops from rollforward.
- K8s RBAC logs suggest the serviceaccount-subject access review returned 'false' once (timed out) before returning 'true' for same check.

Interim reproducer: rerunning the binding lookup against authz-cache while inducing a small TTL expiry reproduces reduced-scope introspection for ~30s.

Action items taken so far:
- Manually warmed authz-cache by pre-populating binding entries for affected runner groups (partial mitigation).
- Reverted a concurrent change in infra/iam that changed a lookup key format (rollback PR merged: infra#8342).
- Temporarily paused automated rollforward until fix is rolled out.
comments: Diego Ramos (reporter) 2024-11-15: Noticed multiple release pipelines queueing and failing with similar 403s after the scheduled rollforward. Posting initial investigation notes.
Maya Liu (assignee) 2024-11-15: Assigned and investigating authz-cache behavior; requesting SRE to provide redis latency graphs and Vault audit events.

SRE (Jordan Park) 2024-11-15: Redis cluster saw short GC/eviction cycles at 08:09 UTC — forwarding graphs to this ticket: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/redis/cluster-overview?panel=12
Suspect heavy write storm from rollforward job caused transient key miss.
Release Eng (Asha Patel) 2024-11-15: Paused rollforward job schedule and started manual revert of the infra lookup key format change; will coordinate with infra PR author.

Maya Liu 2024-11-16: Added temporary pre-warming step to rollforward runbook; still seeing rare repro in a controlled staging run. Planning a patch to make token-introspect resilient to partial cache misses.

Security (Sam Green) 2024-11-17: Confirmed no privilege escalation; all tokens observed had correct aud/iss claims. Recommend improving reconciliation between token-issuer and cache propagation window.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: paused automated rollforward and added cache pre-warm + short sleep between rewrap and binding writes to avoid write storm. Permanent fix: update token-introspect flow to fall back to authoritative binding lookup (datastore) when cache returns a miss and harden cache write path with retries and backoff.

Rollout notes:
- Patch merged to infra (PR infra#8370) that adds datastore fallback and retries for authz-cache reads.
- Deployed to staging 2024-11-17; ran the monthly rollforward in staging with no regressions.
- Production deployment scheduled 2024-11-18 02:00 UTC with monitoring playbook in place.

Follow-ups:
- Add post-rollforward verification step (token-scope smoke test) to runbook.
- Update runbook to include cache pre-warm and jittered write schedule.
- Track and set alert for authz-cache miss rate above 0.5% during roll operations.
resolution_status: Fix deployed to staging, prod rollout scheduled
